- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., post-70+ values), often overshooting by 2–5%.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum; true values often rise faster than forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects downward after strong upward moves, then fails to recover.
- Horizon-specific: last 5–7 days of forecast tend to be more accurate, suggesting model struggles with short-term volatility.
- Avoids sharp downward corrections; underestimates volatility in the middle of the forecast window.
